title: Peter Bocage, Dorsey's band and teacher Charlie DeVergis
summary: Tom speaks of violinist Peter Bocage and his father, Dorsey's band personnel, and Charlie DeVergis who only taught.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Peter's about the only one who still plays much. Who that? Peter Boccage. He still plays violin. Who? Peter Boccage. Oh yeah, yeah, he plays violin. Yeah, yeah.
He plays nice, yeah. Yeah, oh he's a good violin player. Yeah, he's a good violin player, Peter.
Yeah. His daddy used to play a ghetto with Dorsey in the R.J.'s. Is it one of you who don't know Dorsey in the R.J.'s? He used to have a band? I never knew him.

Dorsey had a band. His father used to play ghetto. And Norm Manelon used to play cornet. And Louis DeRouques used to play cornet, two cornets. And Dave Poggins playing trombone. Cantrell playing drums. And Albert Gabriel playing clarinet. Did you know Charlie DeVergis over there? Charlie DeVergis, yeah. He was teaching over there. Clarinet player?
Did he play out much or did he just teach? He almost didn't teach. Yeah, most he'd teach.
Yeah, he'd teach. He used to, you know what he called a fest, he used to teach everything. Piano, everything you want.
Trombone, clarinet, you used to. Yeah.
Yeah. Clarinet, any kind of sort of.
But did he, was he ever a member of a band?
No, I don't remember no, he was a member of no band. Yeah. No. No, no, no, no, no, no band. I never, I never seen him play in the band, he always was a teacher.
Oh, yeah. Who was that saxophone player up there that was a barber? Way, way back. You told Bill about him once. Uh, was a barber?
